tables.title: Comparison between DCS-SOMP and Adaptive DCS-SOMP.
notes: Equation (27) defines RMSE: ε = √[ (1/Q) Σ_{i=1}^Q (p_i − p̂_i)² ]
Q is the number of runs, p_i is the actual value of the chosen parameter at the i-th run, and p̂_i is the estimated value of the chosen parameter at the i-th run.

tables.title: Comparison of RMSE between DCS-SOMP and adaptive DCS-SOMP.
notes: ε_φᶜˢ, ε_φᶜˡ, ε_θᶜˢ, ε_θᶜˡ, and ε_τ represent the RMSE for azimuth AoD, elevation AoD, azimuth AoA, elevation AoA, and ToA, respectively.
The RMSE was determined from 100 runs of each method, considering the average across all paths.

observations: Table 3 compares computational cost (time and operations) between DCS-SOMP and Adaptive DCS-SOMP.
Table 4 compares RMSE values for five parameters (azimuth AoD, elevation AoD, azimuth AoA, elevation AoA, ToA) between the two methods.
Adaptive DCS-SOMP shows significantly lower time (0.88 s vs 84.63 s), fewer mathematical operations (1.4697 × 10⁹ vs 4.0393 × 10⁹), and lower RMSE across all five parameters compared to DCS-SOMP.
The text states that RMSE ε is calculated as in Equation (27), with Q = number of runs, p_i = actual value, p̂_i = estimated value at i-th run.
The RMSE values in Table 4 were determined from 100 runs per method, averaging across all paths.
uncertainties: The exact definition of subscripts 'c^s' and 'c^l' (e.g., coarse/soft vs coarse/long?) is not explicitly defined in the visible text; only their mapping to parameters (azimuth AoD, etc.) is given.
No standard deviations or confidence intervals are reported for RMSE values in Table 4 — only point estimates.
The phrase 'the non-adaptive method' in the paragraph after Table 4 refers to DCS-SOMP, but this is interpretive; the table itself labels it as 'DCS-SOMP'.
Equation (27) uses p_i and p̂_i generically, but Table 4 applies it to five distinct parameters — the mapping from generic p_i to specific ε_φᶜˢ etc. is described in text, not in table structure.
